message.content:
In Major League Baseball’s postseason, the **World Series** is the championship round where two league champions face off in a *best‑of‑seven* format.  
- Each side plays up to seven games.  
- A team needs four victories to win the title.  
- If one team reaches four wins before Game 7, the remaining games aren’t scheduled.  

So “who won” depends entirely on how many games were actually completed:

| Scenario | Games Played | Winner |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| One team gets 4–0 | 4 | That team |
| One team gets 4–1 | 5 | That team |
| One team gets 4–2 | 6 | That team |
| One team gets 4–3 | 7 | That team |

If you’re referring to a particular season—say the latest World Series—you’d need the actual results from those games. Once the full set of outcomes is known, simply count the wins per team; whoever has at least four wins takes home the trophy.
